nodes.label: The ten acceptance criteria
nodes.rationale: Mechanism and behaviour are separated deliberately: several criteria are half a property of this code and half a property of a model's judgement, and only the first half can be a cargo test.

nodes.label: cargo-dist deliberately not adopted
nodes.rationale: It would replace release.yml, not extend it: the release process would be described by a tool's defaults rather than a file this repo controls, and the first disagreement is fixed by a version pin instead of an edit. Reconsider at Windows code signing.

nodes.label: xtask deliberately not adopted
nodes.rationale: This repo needs three commands, every contributor already has cargo, and adding a crate to alias them would add a compile step to the gate it is aliasing.

nodes.label: macOS and Windows artifacts never run
nodes.source_location: ## What has and has not actually run
nodes.rationale: The release job proves they build and upload, not that they work. A release checklist that implies more verification than happened is worse than a short one.

nodes.label: Crate version not bumped with the tag
nodes.source_location: ## What has and has not actually run
nodes.rationale: Both releases ship a binary reporting smith 0.1.0, so smith update sees v0.1.01 as newer and will keep offering the same update forever.

nodes.label: macOS Gatekeeper risk for chrome-headless-shell
nodes.source_location: ## What has and has not actually run
nodes.rationale: Downloaded unsigned and unnotarised, so Gatekeeper is expected to refuse it on first run and nothing in smith setup handles that yet.

nodes.label: Package-manager templates (Homebrew, Scoop, installer)
nodes.rationale: Templates carry placeholder checksums until the corresponding GitHub release exists; do not publish an update with placeholder hashes.
